information.content: Alpha-2 agonist sedative/analgesic used mainly in combination protocols for exotic species.
Avoid in unstable cardiovascular disease, pregnancy/diabetes and where vomiting is contraindicated; reverse with atipamezole when needed.
Anticonvulsant used as adjunct or maintenance therapy for refractory seizures in selected exotic species.
Reduce dose in renal or severe hepatic impairment and taper when changing therapy.
Anabolic steroid occasionally used for tissue breakdown or anaemia support where clinically justified.
Avoid breeding, pregnant, immature or diabetic animals; monitor liver and haematology.
Aminoglycoside used mainly topically or orally for gut decontamination rather than systemic therapy.
Systemic absorption/toxicity may occur with ulcerated gut or prolonged/high-dose therapy.
5-HT3 antagonist antiemetic/nausea support used when other antiemetics are inadequate or unsuitable.
Do not use if intestinal obstruction is suspected.
SSRI used for selected behavioural conditions alongside environmental and behavioural therapy.
Delayed onset and interaction potential mean it should not be used as a quick sedation tool.
Topical/intratracheal azole antifungal used for selected dermatophytosis or aspergillosis situations.
Hepatotoxic if swallowed and irritating to eyes; dilution and route are critical.
ACE inhibitor used for CHF, hypertension or proteinuric renal disease support in selected exotics.
Start cautiously and monitor renal values, potassium and blood pressure.
Beta-2 agonist bronchodilator used for bronchospasm support in selected birds and rats.
Can cause tachycardia and arrhythmias; delivery method matters.
Virostatic antiviral prodrug used in selected avian and reptile viral disease situations.
Does not eradicate latent infection and needs diagnostic/outbreak management.
Anticoagulant primarily used in exotics for catheter/cannula patency rather than systemic anticoagulation.
Bleeding risk and unpredictable effect require caution.
Factor Xa-biased anticoagulant; selected avian use includes PTFE toxicosis support.
Bleeding and renal dysfunction are key concerns.
Barbiturate euthanasia agent authorised for multiple exotic species/routes depending product.
Intracardiac use must be under anaesthesia; do not use euthanasia solution for seizure control.
Antiprotozoal used rarely in ferrets for Pneumocystis pneumonia.
Toxicity risk to kidney/liver and injection site injury are important.
Barbiturate anticonvulsant used for seizure management in selected exotic species.
Serum concentration and hepatic monitoring are valuable where feasible.
Bromide anticonvulsant used in ferrets alone or with phenobarbital.
Chloride intake and fluids alter bromide excretion.
Anthelmintic used for GI nematodes in selected mammals, reptiles and amphibians.
Repeat dosing should reflect parasite life cycle and diagnostics.
Irreversible alpha blocker used in ferrets for urethral spasm/reflex dyssynergia.
First-dose hypotension is a real possibility.
Non-selective beta blocker used for selected cardiac tachyarrhythmias/cardiomyopathy.
Avoid in bradyarrhythmia, decompensated CHF or bronchospasm-prone patients.
Antifolate antiprotozoal used for toxoplasmosis/plasmodium-type infections in selected species.
Bone marrow suppression and folate handling need attention.
Urinary alkaliniser and potassium source used in selected urolith/metabolic cases.
Avoid renal impairment/cardiac disease and monitor potassium.
Topical ocular local anaesthetic used for examination/procedures.
Not for therapeutic repeat use and should not be applied before Schirmer tear testing.
Macrolide antibiotic for susceptible infections where stewardship supports use.
Avoid oral use in small herbivores due fatal enterotoxaemia risk.
Lincosamide antibiotic for susceptible infections in selected species.
Avoid in small herbivores/hamsters; GI and hepatic adverse effects matter.

Severe hypotension, cardiac output failure, hyperkalaemia or severe renal perfusion compromise.
Major bleeding, thrombocytopenia or high haemorrhage risk.

Use of euthanasia solution for seizure control or IM administration.

Therapeutic repeat use for ocular pain/ulcer management.
